---
title: producerlifecycle
description: "Keep goroutine producers bounded by their receivers."
---

import CheckIdentity from '../../../site/src/components/CheckIdentity.astro';

## What it detects

Reports producer goroutines that can block after their receiver stops waiting.

### Checks

{/* gohawk:generated-checks:start */}
| Check | Kind | Tier | What it detects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <CheckIdentity name="abandoned-send" tier="core" /> | hazard | core | Reports producer goroutines that can block after their receiver stops waiting. |
{/* gohawk:generated-checks:end */}

## Why this is flagged

A producer goroutine that sends on an unbuffered channel blocks until something
receives. If the consumer stops early — an error, an early return, a cancelled
context — a producer that keeps trying to send has no one to receive it and
blocks forever, leaking the goroutine and whatever it holds. Making the send
cancellation-aware, or draining the channel, gives the producer a way to stop.

Further reading: [Go concurrency patterns: Pipelines and cancellation](https://go.dev/blog/pipelines).

## How to fix it

Drain every result, provide a proven buffer, or make sends cancellation-aware.

## Examples

{/* gohawk:generated-examples:start */}
### Flagged code

```go gohawk=""
func firstResultOnly() error {
  results := make(chan error)
  go func() {
    results <- errors.New("first")
    results <- errors.New("second")
  }()
  return <-results
}
```

### Accepted code

```go
func drainResults() {
  results := make(chan error)
  go func() {
    results <- errors.New("first")
    results <- errors.New("second")
  }()
  <-results
  <-results
}
```
{/* gohawk:generated-examples:end */}
